sections.name: Pranav PT
bio_paragraphs: I became a CA in 2019. I thought I was good at Excel. I was wrong — and that humbling was the best thing that ever happened to me.
Over the next two years, I taught myself VBA, then Python, then Git, then AI — entirely on my own, while working full-time in government finance. Not because it was required. Because I was curious.

In 2021, I made my first GitHub commit and posted my first YouTube video. I wanted to tell the Finance world that building technology is not a skill reserved for Computer Science graduates. It's a skill anyone can learn.
Today, I teach Finance professionals and students how to automate their work, build their own tools, and understand technology from the inside out.

events.title: Qualified CA — All India Rank 5
events.description: Finished the CA journey. Entered the professional world full of confidence. Thought I was good at Excel.

events.title: Left EY with false confidence
events.description: Walked out of EY thinking I knew everything about spreadsheets. I did not.

events.title: Joined IOCL — Financial Reporting
events.description: Started working at Indian Oil Corporation in Bihar & Jharkhand Finance Operations. Giant company. Massive numbers. Massive amounts of repetitive work.

events.title: Attended trainings. Realized how little I knew.
events.description: Sat through Excel training sessions and discovered capabilities of the tool I had been using daily but barely scratched the surface of. The humbling began.

events.title: Decided to learn VBA Macro
events.description: Too much repetitive work. There had to be a better way. Started learning VBA — the first step into automation.

events.title: Hit a wall in VBA. Found Python.
events.description: VBA had limits. Someone mentioned Python. Downloaded it. Started learning. The world opened up.

events.title: Realized coders are not a different breed.
events.description: Months of self-teaching made something click: this is just logic. Anyone can learn this. Coders are not born — they just started earlier.

events.title: Made my life's first GitHub commit
events.description: Built an Office Assistant — a tool to prevent uploading files to third-party websites, keeping sensitive data in-house. Felt like discovering the future of Finance.

events.title: Presented the idea at IOCL. Crickets.
events.description: Presented the concept of an in-house Office Assistant to the company. The idea didn't get much attention. That was okay. The learning mattered more.

events.title: Posted my first YouTube video
events.description: Decided to tell the Finance world: making apps is possible, and coding is a learnable skill — even if you're not a developer.

events.title: Posted my first 'AI for Finance' video
events.description: One line. One submission: AI in 2021 is the same as the internet in 1995. Most people dismissed it. A few got it.

events.title: Building. Teaching. Growing.
events.description: What followed was four years of consistent work.
milestones_in_period: 20+ apps built for Finance — covering GST, document management, automation workflows
Numerous corporate training sessions on Finance Automation, Python & AI
Built the first DPDP Act Compliant Document Management System for a CA Firm
Working on a Client Portal for CA Students
Running Weekend + Weekday batches: Automation with Python + AI
Building a community of 'Unconventional CAs' who want to pursue technology as a parallel career

events.title: Still learning. Still building. Still teaching.
events.description: 6,000+ community members. The mission is the same: prove that technology is learnable — and worth learning.
